info.title: notefeed API
info.description:
Post markdown notes to a feed, read them back. See https://docs.notefeed.me/

Every error is JSON, `{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`. Besides the responses listed per operation, an unknown path under /api/v1 answers 404 (`not_found`) and a method an operation doesn't have answers 405 with `Allow`.

tags.name: Feeds
tags.description: By the feed's name, the write key. Need the instance password when one is set.

tags.name: Read
tags.description: By the feed's read id. Public and read-only.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Where accounts are on: what the account signed in on this instance's pages owns, and its tokens. A request with an account token (`Authorization: Bearer nf_…`) acts as its account on every Feeds operation.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: A file sent apart from the MCP call that posts it, to a short-lived URL whose token is its only credential.

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description: Where licenses are sold: what they cost, where to buy them and where buyers manage them. Public.

post.description: The body is the note, a file, and `Content-Type` says which kind: `text/markdown` (UTF-8, at most 102400 bytes), or an image, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp` (at most NOTEFEED_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES as sent, default 10 MiB). Nothing is guessed: any other type, or none, is `415`, and so is a body that is not what the type says (an image is recognized by its first bytes; SVG is refused). Markdown is stored byte for byte. An image is stored processed, not as sent: turned the way its EXIF orientation says, scaled to at most 2560 px on its long side, encoded again in its own format (JPEG and WebP at quality 85, PNG lossless, an animated GIF or WebP keeps its frames), and without metadata (EXIF, GPS position, XMP, comments). Send it full size; one of more than 100 megapixels is `413`, and a body that does not decode as the image it declares is `415`. Creates the feed with its first note, optionally protected by its own password (`X-Feed-Password`; 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end) and with the read id in `X-Read-Id`; both are only used by the post that creates the feed. Where licenses are sold, a post that creates a feed with a password, or with pictures, needs an account (its token, or signed in on this instance's pages) whose license covers one more feed: the new feed goes under it; else `402`. Posting to a protected feed needs its password. Also served at `POST /{feed}`, the short form curl one-liners use. The response names the note's `file` and where it is served, `file_url`, under the feed's read id (public like the read link). Metadata goes in headers: `X-Note-Title`, `X-Note-Tags` (at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed), `X-Note-Alt` (images), `X-Note-Name` (the original file name), `X-Note-Date` (where it is placed in the feed: a past date backdates it, a future one schedules it), `X-Note-Draft` (`true`: a draft, which readers do not see until it is published), `X-Note-Language` (the note's language; a single `lang:` tag sets it when it is not given, and is then not stored as a tag). A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Several pictures may have the same file name (a phone calls every photo `image.jpg`): each is stored, and they are appended, but a text that refers to such a name is 400. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. The `text` part is optional: `X-Note-Title` goes on the text note, `X-Note-Tags` on every note, `X-Note-Date` and `X-Note-Language` on the text note (its pictures take the milliseconds just before it); with no `text` part only the pictures are stored, each with the title, and the answer's top level is the first picture. A refused multipart post that would have created a protected feed creates nothing.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: The feed's name. It is the write key: anyone who knows it can post.

parameters.name: X-Feed-Password
parameters.description: The feed's own password, when it has one: to post, list or get, and (as the current password) to change or remove it. On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

parameters.name: X-Read-Id
parameters.description: The read id the feed gets when this post creates it: 3 to 64 characters (a-z, 0-9, - and _), random when left out or empty, ignored for a feed that exists. A short readable one is guessable: protect the feed with a password if that matters. 409 when it is taken

parameters.name: X-Note-Title
parameters.description: The note's title: at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused). Left out or empty, a markdown note is titled by its text. Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Sender
parameters.description: Who posted the note, as shown on it: at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused). Not verified. It wins over the signed-in name; left out or empty, the signed-in name, if any. Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Tags
parameters.description: The note's tags (`ci`, `deploy`): at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed. Not verified; readers see them. Comma-separated; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Alt
parameters.description: A picture's alternative text: at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused). For image notes only. Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Name
parameters.description: The note's file name (at most 200 characters; `/`, `\` and control characters are dropped): for a picture, its original name. The read link serves the newest note with that name at `/r/{readId}/{name}`, a stable address for a file that changes (a name ending in a lower-case extension, such as `post-to-notefeed.md`); a note's own file name (`<id>.<ext>`) comes first. Not unique. Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Language
parameters.description: The note's language, a BCP 47 language tag (`de`, `en`, `pt-BR`): letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 35 characters; stored with the language lower-case, a region upper-case and a script title-case. Readers' pages and feeds mark the note with it. Left out or empty: none. A single `lang:<language>` tag sets it when it is not given (the tag is then not stored). Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Date
parameters.description: The note's date: an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset (`2026-10-01T09:30:00Z`) or a date alone (midnight UTC), from 1970 to 9999. The note takes its place in the feed by it; a time after now schedules it: readers see it from then on. Its attachments move with it. Left out or empty: now. Sent as UTF-8; empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Draft
parameters.description: A draft: only whoever can post to the feed sees it, readers do not until it is published. Its pictures follow it. Left out or false: published.

put.summary: Send the file of an upload
put.description: The URL of an upload that the MCP tool `create_upload` made (#381): its body is the file's raw bytes (`curl -T file <url>`), of the type the upload was made for; `Content-Type` is not read. The token in the path is the only credential: no instance password, feed password or account. The URL takes one file, within 15 minutes of being made; a refused file may be sent again. The file is then posted by the upload's id, over MCP (`post_file`, `post_note`'s attachments, `set_feed_image`), which runs every check of a post and deletes the upload. Over REST, a post takes the file in its own body, so there is no upload to make.

parameters.description: The upload's token, from its upload_url

413.description: Larger than the upload takes: NOTEFEED_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES for an image, 102400 bytes for markdown

put.description: The body is the new file, with the same rules as posting: a `Content-Type` that is one of the accepted types, a body that is what it declares. A note keeps its type, so the type must be the note's own (`415` otherwise). An image is stored processed, not as sent: turned the way its EXIF orientation says, scaled to at most 2560 px on its long side, encoded again in its own format (JPEG and WebP at quality 85, PNG lossless, an animated GIF or WebP keeps its frames), and without metadata (EXIF, GPS position, XMP, comments). Send it full size; one of more than 100 megapixels is `413`, and a body that does not decode as the image it declares is `415`. Id, creation time and metadata stay: the title of a markdown note without one set follows the new text. Change the title, alt text or tags with `PATCH`. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't edit. A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Several pictures may have the same file name (a phone calls every photo `image.jpg`): each is stored, and they are appended, but a text that refers to such a name is 400. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. On a `PUT` the `text` part is required and the note must be a markdown note; the note keeps its own title and tags, `X-Note-Tags` goes on the new pictures. A raw body ignores `X-Note-Tags`. The note is looked up first: a missing note is `404` and an image note `415` whatever the body holds.

An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

patch.summary: Change a note's title, alt text, tags, language or date
patch.description: Sets the note's title, alt text (only for images), tags, language and/or date. An empty title, alt or language removes it: a markdown note's title follows its text again. `tags` replaces the whole list (an empty list removes them), with the same rules as on a post; a single `lang:` tag in it sets the language when that is not given. A new date moves the note in the feed, with its attachments; a date after now schedules it. Id and links stay, and so does its RSS item's guid. At least one is needed. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't change notes.

On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

get.summary: Get one of the feed's files
get.description: A note's file by its own name (`<id>.<ext>`, a note's `file`), for whoever may post to the feed: also a draft's or a scheduled note's, which the read link (`file_url`) does not serve until readers may see them, so a post with pictures can be checked before it goes out. The body is the file's bytes, with the `Content-Type` of its extension and an `ETag` (`If-None-Match` gives `304`). Files by any other name, as the read link has them, are not served here.

On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

post.summary: Create a feed without posting a note
post.description: Reserves the feed name now (ADR 0047): with a password it is protected from its first moment, with a read id it gets that read link. Where licenses are sold it needs an account (its token, or signed in on this instance's pages) whose license covers one more feed, and the new feed goes under it; free feeds start with their first note. A feed that exists is 409. Counts against the post rate limit and the instance's feed cap, like a first post. After it, change the title and description with updateFeed.

put.description: Replaces both the title (at most 100 characters) and the description (at most 500); surrounding whitespace is trimmed and control and text-direction override characters are refused. `show_sender` (default true) shows who posted each note to readers; omitted leaves it as it is. `read_id` gives the feed another read link (3 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _; empty for a random one): the old id is freed and answers like an unknown read id until another feed takes it, and the notes are not edited (a relative image link follows the new id, a full URL does not). A short readable read id is guessable, so protect the feed with a password if that matters. An instance can turn chosen read ids off (NOTEFEED_ALLOW_CUSTOM_IDS=0): then only an empty `read_id` is accepted. `image` is the file name `uploadImage` returned for this feed (title image), empty to remove it, or omitted to leave it as it is; any other value is a 400. `name` renames the feed (#350), after everything else is saved: the answer is the feed under its new name, and the old name answers like any unused one from then on. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Only on a feed that exists: it is created by its first note. Read links can't change settings.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: The feed's name. It is the write key: anyone who knows it can post.

parameters.name: X-Feed-Password

On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

sender.description: Who posted the note, as shown on it: at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused). Not verified. Empty removes it.

tags.description: The note's tags (`ci`, `deploy`): at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed. Not verified; readers see them. The whole new list; empty removes them, left out keeps them.

language.description: The note's language, a BCP 47 language tag (`de`, `en`, `pt-BR`): letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 35 characters; stored with the language lower-case, a region upper-case and a script title-case. Readers' pages and feeds mark the note with it. Empty removes it.

date.description: The note's date: an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset (`2026-10-01T09:30:00Z`) or a date alone (midnight UTC), from 1970 to 9999. The note takes its place in the feed by it; a time after now schedules it: readers see it from then on. Its attachments move with it.

draft.description: A draft: only whoever can post to the feed sees it, readers do not until it is published. Its pictures follow it. false publishes it, true hides it from readers again (refused while a picture of it is the feed's title image); its date stays.

password.description: The new password: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end
A password that protects the new feed: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end. Empty or left out: an open feed

read_id.description: The read id to give the feed (3 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, - and _); left out: a random one

title.description: Display title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty means none (the feed's name is shown)

description.description: Description, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); may be empty

image.description: The file name of an image uploaded to this feed (see uploadImage), shown as the feed's title image; empty removes it, omitted leaves it as it is

show_sender.description: Whether readers (RSS, the read API and pages) see who posted each note; omitted leaves it as it is, a new feed starts with true

sender_name.description: What the owner's own notes show as their sender, when posted by the owner's account without a sender of their own; changing it changes it on all of them. One line, at most 100 characters; empty shows none. Only the feed's owner may change it (403, code `owner_only`); omitted leaves it as it is

read_id.description: A new read id (3 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _), empty for a random one; omitted leaves it as it is. The old read link stops showing this feed, and may later show another one. Notes are not edited: a relative image link (`![](file)`) follows the new id, a full URL keeps the old one and is yours to change. Reserved feeds keep theirs. 409 when it is taken

name.description: A new name for the feed (1 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _); omitted, empty or the current one leaves it as it is. Everything goes with it: notes, files, settings, password, license and read link. The old name stops working at once and is free: a post to it later creates a new feed, without an error. Change NOTEFEED_FEED, CI secrets, scripts and MCP configurations before they next run (a browser that unlocked the feed unlocks it again). A short name is guessable: protect the feed with a password if that matters. Reserved feeds keep theirs. 409 when it is taken

notes.description: The feed's notes now: texts, images and the operator's marks alike

cap.description: How many notes a free feed keeps; past it, each new note drops the oldest one, of any kind

title.description: Display title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty means none (the feed's name is shown)

description.description: Description, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); may be empty

protected.description: Whether the feed has its own password

owned.description: Whether the feed belongs to an account (its owner): then only the owner manages its passwords, renames and deletes it

yours.description: Whether it belongs to the account signed in with this request

read_url.description: The feed's read-only RSS link; null while the feed has no notes, or if the server can't read the feed's stored read id

atom_url.description: The same feed as Atom (RFC 4287), beside the RSS link; null exactly when read_url is

image_url.description: The feed's title image (absolute URL, served under the read id), or null

show_sender.description: Whether readers see who posted each note

sender_name.description: What the owner's own notes show as their sender; empty for none (see updateFeed)

shortcut_url.description: The iPhone Shortcut "Send to notefeed": opened on an iPhone, it adds notefeed to the share sheet; at setup it asks for the server's address, this feed's name, its password and, optional, the server password

free_tier.description: A feed without a license on an instance that sells them: its notes against the free tier's cap. null when no cap applies (a licensed feed, or an instance that sells no licenses)

title.description: Display title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty means none (the feed's name is shown)

description.description: Description, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); may be empty

image_url.description: The feed's title image (absolute URL, served under the read id), or null

period.description: How long one payment lasts; the license renews until cancelled

name.description: The plan's name, as the payment provider holds it

description.description: The plan's description from the payment provider, possibly empty

amount.description: The price per period in the currency's smallest unit (cents)

plans.description: What is sold right now, monthly then yearly; empty while the payment provider can't be read

buy_url.description: The license page: a person signed in to an account buys there, for as many feeds as they choose

manage_url.description: The account page, where the account's holder manages its license and opens the payment provider's portal

manage.description: How managing a purchase works, in a sentence to show a person

password.description: A protected feed: one of its passwords. An open feed: the password it gets now, as setting one does (1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end)

type.description: The media type the upload was made for

id.description: The password's id, to revoke it

name.description: What it is for, as the owner named it ("blog script", "Anna"); a feed's password from before it had an owner is "Feed password"

created.description: When it was added (ISO 8601); null for the one from before the feed had an owner

id.description: The password's id, to revoke it

name.description: What it is for, as the owner named it ("blog script", "Anna"); a feed's password from before it had an owner is "Feed password"

created.description: When it was added (ISO 8601); null for the one from before the feed had an owner

password.description: The password, 24 characters: shown only this once. Send it as X-Feed-Password

name.description: What it is for: one line, 1 to 50 characters

feeds.description: The names of the feeds the account owns, sorted

valid_until.description: When its paid period ends (ms since the epoch), or null

active.description: Whether it is paid for now

units.description: How many feeds the active subscriptions cover together

covered.description: The account's feeds put under the license, oldest first

licensed.description: Those it covers now: the first `units` of `covered`

units.description: The new number of feeds, 1 to 100

id.description: The token's id, to revoke it

scope.description: `read`: only reading requests; `read+write`: everything the account may do

last_used.description: When it was last used (ISO 8601), or null

id.description: The token's id, to revoke it

scope.description: `read`: only reading requests; `read+write`: everything the account may do

last_used.description: When it was last used (ISO 8601), or null

token.description: The token, shown only this once: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the REST API

name.description: What it is for: one line, 1 to 50 characters

days.description: How long it works, 1 to 365 days; default 90

password.description: The instance password (NOTEFEED_PASSWORD), when one is set; on an instance with accounts, an account token (`nf_…`) instead
